question.worked_solution:
First, we expand the parentheses on both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3(1-p) & =4(p+1) \\ -3\cdot 1+3\cdot p & =4\cdot p+4\cdot 1 \\ -3+3p & =4p+4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we must bring all variables to one side of the equation and all constants to the other side. 

Notice that we have $3p$ on the left-hand side and $4p$ on the right-hand side. Since the variable on the right-hand side has a larger coefficient, let's bring all the variables to this side. 

The first step is to remove the $3p$ from the left-hand side of the equation. We do this by subtracting $3p$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3+3p & =4p+4 \\ -3+3p-3p & =4p+4-3p \\ -3 & =p+4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we remove the $4$ from the right-hand side. We do this by subtracting $4$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3 & =p+4 \\ -3-4 & =p+4-4 \\ -7 & =p \\ p & =-7\end{aligned}
$$
